arguments.value: S. Maurice Hicks, Jr., born in 1952 in New Orleans, Louisiana, is a United States district judge for the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Louisiana, a position to which he was nominated by President George W. Bush in 2003 and confirmed by the Senate later that year. He earned his B.A. from Texas Christian University in 1974 and his J.D. from Louisiana State University Law School in 1977. Before joining the federal bench, he served as a law clerk and staff attorney for the Louisiana Legislative Council and then practiced privately in Shreveport from 1977 to 2003. He served as chief judge of the district court from 2017 to 2022 and was a member of the Judicial Conference of the United States from 2020 to 2023.
